target_customer: Banks, fintechs, insurers and digital businesses in Indonesia that must verify customer identity
problem: Digital onboarding in Indonesia needs fast, accurate identity verification and fraud prevention, but verification data and tooling lagged the shift to digital services.
business_model: B2B SaaS and API usage-based identity verification
product_category: Identity verification, face recognition and deepfake detection

founders.name: Williem
founders.background_notes: Named as a founder in the TechCrunch headline caption; YC page lists no founders.

founders.name: Rick Firnando
founders.background_notes: Named as a founder in the TechCrunch caption and as CEO in a December 2024 detikInet article.

technical_complexity.rationale: Building face recognition and liveness models that rank well in NIST tests and run at bank scale needs real machine learning expertise.

defensibility.rationale: NIST-evaluated models, bank integrations and local compliance (OJK, data protection) raise switching costs, though other Indonesian vendors offer similar services.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Competing vendors exist but no acquisition of Verihubs was found.

market_need_then: The YC page cites pandemic-driven digital acceleration and unmet verification needs; the company reports serving over 300 companies at the time of the batch and more than 400 clients later.

identity.voice_and_tone: Direct and protective ('Stop Them Before They Take Everything')

branding.brand_signature: Claims of top NIST ranking in Indonesia

brand_strength.rationale: A B2B trust brand with NIST and bank customer proof points; no community or brand-led growth evidence.

outcome_analysis: Verihubs raised a $2.8M seed in September 2021 led by Insignia Venture Partners and grew into an identity verification vendor for Indonesian banks and insurers, later adding deepfake detection in late 2024. It is active with 63 staff and more than 400 clients; no later priced round was found.
notes: Seed confirmed by TechCrunch, e27 and DailySocial (39.9 billion rupiah). CB Insights lists about 2.93M across five rounds including a 2022 accelerator round; unverified. Founders taken from a TechCrunch article title caption and a detik article; education and employers not found. Competitors VIDA, ADVANCE.AI, Nodeflux and Asli RI appear only in current-day sources, not dated to 2021, so the list is empty. Founding year 2019 comes from CB Insights.
